You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The issue occurs in the Base64InputStream class during multiple calls to the read() method with encoding enabled. The test calls read() repeatedly on a Base64InputStream constructed with a Codec105ErrorInputStream underlying stream and encoding enabled (doEncode = true).

Looking at the read() method in Base64InputStream, it calls the overloaded read(byte[], int, int) method with params to read one byte at a time. The read(byte[], int, int) method has a loop that continues trying to read data through the Base64 class (base64.readResults()) until it returns a non-zero number of bytes read.

Inside this read(byte[], int, int) method:
- If base64.hasData() is false, it reads some bytes from the underlying stream into a temporary buffer.
- If encoding is enabled (doEncode = true), it calls base64.encode(...) with the newly read bytes.

Looking at the Base64.encode(byte[], int, int) implementation:
- It maintains a modulus that increments modulo 3 for every byte encoded.
- For every 3 bytes (when modulus == 0), it encodes 4 base64 bytes into the output buffer.
- When EOF is detected (inAvail < 0), it encodes the final few bytes and adds padding according to the modulus value.
- The encoding buffers are resized if necessary.

The root cause indicated by the exception "ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 2 at Base64.encode" suggests that the encode() method is trying to write to a position outside the bounds of its buffer array. 

One suspicious part is the assumption about the size of the buffer and its adjustments:
- The encode() method expects the buffer large enough to accommodate encoded output.
- The Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) method calls base64.setInitialBuffer(b, offset, len) if the read from the underlying stream returned c > 0 and the output buffer length equals requested length.
- This initial buffer might be used as the internal buffer for encoding output.

The error indicates that when encoding a large stream byte-by-byte, after many calls to read(), the buffer in Base64.encode is apparently too small or wrongly positioned, causing an index to go out of bounds.

Therefore, the bug happens because Base64InputStream's logic for allocating or setting the output buffer for encoding is not correctly maintaining or resizing the internal buffer in the Base64 encoder. The buffer may be too small for the encoded output (which can be larger than input), or the position/index counters (such as pos) used during encoding get out of sync with the buffer length, causing the out-of-bounds access.

This is consistent with the report's observation of failure after many successful read() calls (more than 10,920 reads), meaning the buffer management fails over time under heavy encoding load.

Recent bug reports do not point to the same buffer-index error, so this appears to be a new issue related to how Base64InputStream handles the buffers and passes them to Base64 for encoding.

Summary: The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException occurs because the Base64 encoder's internal buffer is too small or not properly resized when encoding large streams on demand via Base64InputStream.read(). The buffer management logic either in Base64InputStream.read() or Base64.encode() is faulty and results in invalid memory access on the buffer array.

Next steps:
- Inspect Base64InputStream's use of base64.setInitialBuffer(...) and how it manages its own buffer arrays.
- Inspect how Base64.encode() resizes buffers when needed.
- Check interaction between Base64InputStream and Base64 for buffer handling during encoding.

This explanation covers why repeated read() calls on an encoding Base64InputStream eventually causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inside Base64.encode().

This detailed analysis should pinpoint the buffer size management in encoding as the source of the bug.
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
